DELIVERABLES_VERIFIED_PAGE_BY_PAGE.verdict: ALL FOUR ARE REAL, SUBSTANTIVE AND HONEST. No stubs, no padding, no promises of a guaranteed Etsy reinstatement anywhere.

MY_ERROR_AND_ITS_CORRECTION.what_I_did_wrong: cycle 118 noticed the Gumroad file was 166,634 bytes while the local verified PDF was 122,465 bytes, and treated the mismatch as a defect. In this cycle I acted on that judgement and REPLACED the live 166,634-byte file with the 122,465-byte PDF.
MY_ERROR_AND_ITS_CORRECTION.why_it_was_wrong: I judged by byte size alone. The 166,634-byte file is books/etsy_suspension_appeal_kit_v2_bundle.zip, which contains exactly what the live description promises. My replacement had REDUCED delivery from four pieces to one while the description still promised four.
MY_ERROR_AND_ITS_CORRECTION.how_it_was_caught: the update_product_file() re-read returned the full product record, whose description explicitly says '4 files in one download'. Comparing the description against the attached file exposed the contradiction immediately.
MY_ERROR_AND_ITS_CORRECTION.correction: the bundle was re-uploaded in the same cycle and verified by an independent re-read: files=[166634], file_info '163 KB', price $29 unchanged, published True, zip integrity OK, 5 parts.
MY_ERROR_AND_ITS_CORRECTION.net_effect_on_the_seller: none. The product ended this cycle exactly as it began, with the correct bundle attached. No customer was affected and no sale was lost.
MY_ERROR_AND_ITS_CORRECTION.lesson_recorded: a byte-size difference is not evidence of a defect. The correct comparison is description-claims versus deliverable-contains, which is what I should have run first.
